transcription_uncertainties.issue: The lexeme can denote thousand or, in explicitly quantified contexts, ten thousand. Thousand is the supported critical rendering here because actualDillmann721subsection1 specifically citesHen10,19; this is not an unqualified universal numeralidentity or independentmanuscriptconsensus.
Press-measure metonymy retained; no exact moderncapacity/conversion supplied.

translation.text: Every delightful tree will be planted on it, and vineyards will be planted on it. The vine planted on it will produce wine in abundance. Every seed sown on it—one measure will produce a thousand;[a] and one measure of olives will produce ten press-measures of oil.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected wordእልፈhas more than one numerical use. Actual Dillmann1865col721, entryእልፍsubsection1, placesEnoch10:19under “thousand”; subsection2 distinguishes explicit “ten thousand/myriad” uses elsewhere. This qualified rendering follows the verse-specific citation, rather than treating the word as an unambiguous ten thousand. It describes the text’s promised abundance, not a verified agricultural yield.

The unusual olive/oil term is checked in actualDillmann719–720; the press term at873can name a pressing-place or apparatus. “Press-measures” retains the production-capacity image without inventing a modern volume or agricultural technique. The printed press-count፲is ten and is not changed by the separate seed-yield ambiguity.
